Lessons.Title: Equivalent Fractions on the Number Line
ExplanationParagraphs: 2021 Warm-up (10 minutes) Notice and Wonder: Running on a Trail. Tyler and Han each ran part of the SAME trail; invite multiple observations and wonderings about fraction lengths and how a shared whole is essential. The original photograph and teacher discussion are not a fixed numeric assessment.

Activity1 (10 minutes) Running Part of a Trail has exactly THREE pairs of pupil distances, all fractions of the SAME trail: Elena 3/6 vs Han 1/2 ARE EQUAL; Jada 1/4 vs Kiran 2/8 ARE EQUAL; Lin 2/3 vs Mai 5/6 are NOT EQUAL. Show the equal pairs by six-to-two or eight-to-four subdivisions: 3/6=1/2,1/4=2/8. Compare two thirds with four sixths, and five sixths is one extra sixth, so Lin and Mai differ by 1/6 of the trail. The original pupil may use number lines or fraction strips; teacher assesses the drawn comparison and explanation.

Activity2 (10 minutes) Locate and Pair includes ELEVEN original fraction targets in exact sequence: 1/2,1/3,1/4,2/3,2/6,3/8,3/4,4/6,4/8,6/8,7/8. Pupils place ALL eleven as points on one or more number lines and write FOUR paired equations. In the ORIGINAL GIVEN SET exactly the four matching pairs are 1/2=4/8,1/3=2/6,2/3=4/6,3/4=6/8. 1/4,3/8 and7/8 do not have a listed equivalent partner; do not insert a missing 2/8 as if it were in this source set. Optional students may generate NEW further equivalences beyond the prescribed set and justify them.

Activity3 (15 minutes) Rolling for Equivalent Fractions: roll SIX standard number cubes each turn; numbers showing FIVE are WILD CARDS which may count as a chosen number. Find FOUR numbers from the six dice (with legitimate wild replacements) forming a/b=c/d, both denominators nonzero. If not possible, optionally re-roll as many dice as desired, up to TWO re-rolls. The original learner sheet has EIGHT labelled rounds (Round1 through Round8), a free-form explanation per round and one point for each valid equivalent pair. The actual dice rolls and resulting statements are VARIABLE, not fixed source answers; teacher verifies dice provenance, wild-card replacement, re-roll limit and fraction equivalence.

Activity3's scalar equality condition for a/b=c/d is a*d=b*c for nonzero denominators. But a mathematically equal statement not using available rolled digits does NOT satisfy the game rules, and a zero denominator is invalid even with a wildcard. Treat the six original dice, reroll history and explanation as human evidence. No single fixed answer or prefilled dice display is claimed.

Source lesson synthesis ties equivalence on zero-to-one and zero-to-two number lines to same-distance on the shared whole. The owner-device archive gave FOUR distinct source figure URLs with two visually identical 0–1 number-line image files and a 0–2 line. Source Cool-down Equivalence on the Number Line is publisher-gated. The original student task PDF, copyrighted photos, physical dice verification, authoring tests and Stage D remain unverified; first-party diagrams only.

KeyConcepts.Title: Equivalent trail distances
KeyConcepts.Definition: Equal fractions of the SAME trail length represent equal distances.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Fractions a/b and c/d have same value if a*d=b*c.

KeyConcepts.Title: Four equivalent pairs in eleven
KeyConcepts.Definition: A source list can contain fractions with no partner in the same list.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Compare values and pair only original targets; don't fabricate missing source cards.

KeyConcepts.Title: Game valid fractions
KeyConcepts.Definition: Dice-selected numerator and denominator must make actual numbers that compare as equal fractions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: a*d=b*c, with b!=0 and d!=0; also obey which six dice were rolled.
KeyConcepts.Example: A valid dice configuration with 1,2,2,4 can make 1/2=2/4.

KeyConcepts.Title: Student-generated representations
KeyConcepts.Definition: The positions of fractions on a number line depend on a consistent 0–1 unit and equal segments.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Only teacher-inspected diagrams, rolls and explanations can certify source collaborative tasks.
KeyConcepts.Example: 3/8 is a valid fraction mark but has no partner in the given eleven.

WorkedExamples.Title: Elena and Han
WorkedExamples.Question: Did 3/6 and1/2 of the same trail cover equal lengths?
WorkedExamples.Method: Make sixths and count three of them.
Steps: Divide the trail length into six equal intervals.
Three sixths cover half of the same whole.
Han's half ends at the same point.

WorkedExamples.Title: Jada and Kiran
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare1/4 with2/8 of the same trail.
WorkedExamples.Method: Split a fourth into two eighths.
Steps: Both end at same fraction of one whole.

WorkedExamples.Title: Lin and Mai
WorkedExamples.Question: Compare2/3 to5/6.
Steps: Difference is one sixth of the trail.

WorkedExamples.Title: Original four pairs
WorkedExamples.Question: Select four equivalent pairs from the eleven fixed source numbers.
WorkedExamples.Method: Place all values on a common zero-to-one number line, compare positions.
Steps: 3/4 with6/8; other listed values stand alone.

WorkedExamples.Title: Example contingent dice roll
WorkedExamples.Question: Given available rolls 1,2,2,4 plus any two other values, write a valid equality.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use four rolled numbers and check products.
Steps: Teacher confirms digits and any legal wild replacement.
WorkedExamples.Check: Only an illustrative FIRST-PARTY dice example, not original publisher's fixed draw.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claim Lin and Mai ran same distance because denominators can be matched.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Compare four sixths with five sixths; difference one sixth.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: List 1/4=2/8 as one of the four original Activity2 pairs.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: 2/8 does not appear among the eleven Activity2 targets, although it appears in Activity1.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use only the actual original Activity2 set; choose the four provided matching pairs.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Require one correct output per dice round or ignore the five wildcard and two rerolls.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Dice rolls differ; source specifies wild fives and reroll options.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Teacher audits roll record, use of six dice, wild substitution, reroll count and equivalent fractions.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Treat equality as proof a pupil's number-line diagram is properly partitioned.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Numeric ratio check says nothing about drawn equal-distance marks.

SummaryPoints: Original trail comparisons: Elena3/6=Han1/2; Jada1/4=Kiran2/8; Lin2/3 != Mai5/6.
All original 11 Activity2 target fractions preserved; matching four pairs EXACTLY 1/2=4/8,1/3=2/6,2/3=4/6,3/4=6/8.
Rolling for Equivalent Fractions: SIX number cubes, five wild, up to TWO re-rolls, EIGHT source rounds, one point per valid pair.
Teacher reviews diagrams, dice and answers; source Cool-down, PDF, Stage D and academic signoff not certified.
